content: The EXSCEL trial investigated the effects of the once-weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist, exenatide, on cardiovascular outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes. However, the results of this trial did not achieve statistical significance. Despite this, there is robust evidence supporting the cardiovascular benefits of both GLP-1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), multiple cardiovascular risk factors, or diabetic kidney disease. Meta-analyses have demonstrated that GLP-1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors can significantly reduce the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events, lower hospitalization rates, and improve clinical outcomes in high-risk diabetic populations.
